title: Strong unitary designs in optimal depth and space
authors: Teodor Parella-Dilmé, Júlia Barberà-Rodríguez, Salvatore F. E. Oliviero, Antonio A. Mele
abstract: Unitary designs provide finite-moment approximations to Haar-random unitaries, with wide-ranging applications across physics and quantum information, from scrambling and black-hole dynamics to foundational primitives in quantum algorithms. Strong unitary designs capture a more demanding operational notion of approximation, requiring indistinguishability from Haar randomness even for quantum algorithms that may access a unitary not only in the forward direction, but also through its inverse, transpose, and complex conjugate. Motivated by the physical requirement that scrambling arise within the system itself, Schuster, Ma, Lombardi, Brandão, and Huang (arXiv:2509.26310) left open whether strong unitary designs can be generated in logarithmic depth using only the system qubits. For every fixed design order $k$ and measurable-error tolerance, we construct strong approximate unitary $k$-designs in optimal $Θ(\log n)$ all-to-all circuit depth using only the $n$ original system qubits. Our new ingredient is a logarithmic-depth Pauli-mixing bound for the perfect-matching ensemble, whose layers pair the qubits uniformly at random and apply independent random two-qubit gates. This bound controls the mixed forward-reverse two-query case, which we combine with existing design and gluing results to obtain strong unitary designs of arbitrary fixed order.
summary: This theoretical paper addresses the challenge of creating highly accurate approximations of truly random quantum unitaries. By introducing a new Pauli-mixing bound, the authors achieve strong unitary $k$-designs in optimal logarithmic depth ($\Theta(\log n)$). This result is critical for simulating complex physical phenomena like scrambling using limited quantum resources.
main_problem: The primary goal is constructing strong unitary designs that accurately approximate Haar-random unitaries while achieving optimal, low circuit depth.
main_result: The authors successfully construct approximate strong unitary $k$-designs in optimal $\Theta(\log n)$ all-to-all circuit depth using only the original system qubits.
method: The construction relies on a novel logarithmic-depth Pauli-mixing bound for the perfect-matching ensemble, which is combined with existing design and gluing techniques to build high-order designs layer by layer.
model_or_system: The context involves unitary evolution in quantum systems, where strong unitary designs are used as finite-moment approximations to Haar randomness. These designs are crucial for simulating physical processes like scrambling and black-hole dynamics.
key_observables: Measurable error ($	ext{Err}_{	ext{full}}^k(E)$), design order $k$, and the required circuit depth scaling $\Theta(\log n)$.
important_parameters: Design order $k$ and measurable-error tolerance $\epsilon$. The optimal depth scales logarithmically with system size $n$.
main_assumptions: The construction assumes that a logarithmic-depth Pauli-mixing bound can be established for the perfect-matching ensemble, which controls the mixed forward-reverse two-query case.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the quantum comb formalism used to model mixed-query experiments and show the circuit architecture for achieving approximate strong $k$-designs through gluing protocols involving local patches and global shells.
paper_structure: The paper builds upon previous work by first establishing a logarithmic-depth Pauli-mixing bound. It then uses this bound in conjunction with strong gluing lemmas to construct higher-order designs, culminating in the optimal $\Theta(\log n)$ depth result for strong $k$-designs.
why_interesting: This work provides fundamental tools (strong unitary designs) that are essential benchmarks for simulating complex quantum dynamics, such as scrambling rates measured via OTOCs, within realistic circuit constraints.

figures.caption: FIG. 1: A mixed-query distinguisher represented as a quantum comb W. A single unitary U is sampled once from an ensemble and used throughout the experiment: in each of the k slots, the adversary may place an oracle query of U, U †, U T , or U ∗. The comb models the arbitrary operations W1 · · · Wk+1 the distinguisher may apply between queries, and arbitrary retention of quantum memory.

FIG. 2: Architecture of our realization for approximate strong k-designs in measurable error. Each panel resolves a component of the previous one. (a) The strong gluing Lemma 1 upgrades two brickwork macro-layers of local strong k-designs into an extensive strong k-design, after being sandwiched between two global strong 2-design shells (Theorem 3). (b) The strong 2-design shell is realized as a perfect-matching circuit composed with an independent weak relative-error 2-design (Theorem 2). The former controls the mixed-sign query sector, while the latter controls the same-sign sector, both in depth O(log n) for constant error.
